content.text:
For high-spin Mn²⁺ (d⁵), every d–d band is spin-forbidden (⁶A₁g → quartet states). The automatic fitter didn't work here, so I fitted the three bands to the full quartet ligand-field energies by hand.

**Step 1 – The ⁴A₁g/⁴Eg(G) band fixes one combination of B and C**

These two states sit at exactly 10B + 5C above ⁶A₁g, whatever the value of Dq. That is why the band is sharp. So:

10B + 5C = 23 370 cm⁻¹

**Step 2 – The ⁴T₁g(G) and ⁴T₂g(G) bands fix Dq and the B/C split**

The ⁴T₁g(G) and ⁴T₂g(G) energies come from diagonalising the full d⁵ quartet matrices, with 10B + 5C held at 23 370 cm⁻¹. I adjusted Dq and B by hand until the calculated levels matched the bands.

The automatic fitter (`ts_fit_spectrum`) was not used for the answer. It held C at its default of 3850 cm⁻¹ and matched the bands to doublet states. That gave Dq ≈ 2370 cm⁻¹ with a lowest ⁴T₁g near 6400 cm⁻¹, which makes no physical sense for this spectrum.

| Band (assignment) | Observed (cm⁻¹) | Calculated at Dq = 621, B = 773, C = 3128 (cm⁻¹) | Difference (cm⁻¹) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ⁶A₁g → ⁴T₁g(G) | 19 180 | 19 182 | +2 |
| ⁶A₁g → ⁴T₂g(G) | 22 130 | 22 141 | +11 |
| ⁶A₁g → ⁴A₁g, ⁴Eg(G) | 23 370 | 23 370 | 0 |

**Result**
- Dq ≈ 620 cm⁻¹, so 10Dq ≈ 6200 cm⁻¹. This weak field fits an octahedral MnCl₆ chromophore and keeps the ion well inside the high-spin regime.
- B ≈ 773 cm⁻¹. This is about 80 % of the free-ion value for Mn²⁺ (about 960 cm⁻¹), which points to moderately covalent Mn–Cl bonds.
- C ≈ 3130 cm⁻¹, giving C/B ≈ 4.0.

Rounding to Dq ≈ 620 cm⁻¹ changes the calculated bands by only about 10 cm⁻¹. That is far less than the uncertainty in reading the maxima of broad spin-forbidden bands.
